title: Remote Controller
text: A linux-powered radio service device, built on Rock5B and debian, that uploads APRS data while providing web sdr services based on HackRF.
Used to remotely control radio transceivers in HF communications, especially for digital mode such as FT8.
A camera is connected to monitor the status of the transceiver and power supply.
Tx and Rx audio signals are simultaneously forwarded to the web stream, which is useful for live broadcasts.

title: Some RIGs
text: Xiegu G90S, the main HF band transceiver.
Baofeng UV5R, as a portable communication solution when going outside.
QYT KT-8900, as it supports quad-band monitoring, is used as a UHF/VHF band base station at home.
HackRF (not in photo) as a long-term receiver in some special bands.
DKGP10 (two antenna tuning boxes in photo) serves as the primary HF antenna, extended and deployed when needed.
SG7900 antenna (not in photo) is permanently mounted for reception of intra- and inter-urban UHF/VHF signals.
